chapter: Big band, Chicago players, recordings and gospel
title: Gospel feeling in the Catholic choir and a 32-piece jazz mass
summary: He tells of a Catholic choir director and a jazz mass performed with a 32-piece band and 16 singers.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Right, right. Now, like, I belong to the Catholic Church, and the priest there, he was trying his darndest to get a gospel feeling out of the choir.
For many, many years the Church would not allow any instrument except an organ.
And it had to be a pipe organ; they wouldn't even allow an electric organ
It was modified greatly since -- with folk masses and jazz masses.
Mary Lou Williams has written a lot of --

Right, plus he turned very very -- right, and then I have a -- we did it with a 32-piece orchestra, it was a fellow, he was studying to be a minister. And he left and went to Rochester. But he formed a choir. We had a 32-piece band and then about 16 singers. And we did the jazz mass. He wrote one of the jazz masses. And it was terrific.
It was a regular mass, they did the regular service, and all of that, with this jazz band. It was really something.
